speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your gums or other mucous membranes, and small red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand the cause of these symptoms, have you noticed any easy bruising, or does your family history suggest anyone with bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

The clinical presentation of frequent epistaxis, gum bleeding, petechiae, and easy bruising in a 4-year-old male is highly suggestive of a platelet disorder, most commonly Immune Thrombocytopenia.
